patches.old:
As I walked with him, I was glad to see such good things. The shepherd said to me, “Go and bring lime and finely crushed pottery, so that I can fill the hollows left by the stones that were removed and put into the building.[a] Everything around the tower must be made level.”

2. I did as he commanded and brought them to him. “Help me,” he said, “and the work will soon be finished.”[b] He filled the hollows left by the stones that had gone into the building, then ordered that the area around the tower be swept and made clean.

3. The virgins took brooms and swept. They removed all the refuse from the tower and sprinkled water, and the place became cheerful and most fitting for the tower.

4. The shepherd said to me, “Everything has been cleaned. If the master comes to inspect the tower, he will have nothing to blame us for.”[c] After saying this, he wanted to leave.

5. But I caught hold of his bag and began solemnly to implore him by the Lord to explain everything he had shown me.[d] He said to me, “I must be occupied for a little while, and I will explain everything to you. Wait for me here until I return.”

6. I said to him, “Sir, what will I do here by myself?” “You are not by yourself,” he said. “These virgins are with you.” “Then entrust me to them,” I said. The shepherd called them over and said to them, “I entrust this man to you until I return.” Then he left.

7. I was alone with the virgins. They were even more cheerful and friendly toward me, especially the four most glorious among them.

translation:
  text: 'I was glad as I walked with him and saw such good things. The shepherd told me, “Bring lime and
    finely crushed pottery. I will fill the hollows left by the stones that were removed and put into
    the building.[a] Everything around the tower must be level.”


    2. I obeyed and brought them. He said, “Help me, and the work will soon be finished.”[b] He filled
    the hollows left by the stones that had gone into the building. Then he ordered the area around the
    tower to be swept and cleaned.


    3. The virgins took brooms and swept away all the refuse from the tower. They sprinkled water. The
    place became cheerful and most fitting for the tower.


    4. The shepherd said, “Everything has been cleaned. If the master comes to inspect the tower, he will
    have nothing to blame us for.”[c] Then he wanted to leave.


    5. I caught his bag and solemnly begged him by the Lord to explain everything he had shown me.[d]
    He said, “I must be busy for a little while. Then I will explain everything to you. Wait here until
    I return.”


    6. I asked him, “Sir, what will I do here alone?” He said, “You are not alone. The virgins are with
    you.” I said, “Then entrust me to them.” He called them over and said, “I entrust this man to you
    until I return.” Then he left.


    7. I was alone with the virgins. They were even more cheerful and friendly toward me, especially the
    four most glorious among them.'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Removed and put into the building” follows Hilgenfeld’s printed conjecture compared with Latin
      Vulgata. Reported Athos has a differently ordered “fitted into the building and” phrase; the other
      versions are uncertain in the apparatus. The hollows are around the tower where stones had lain,
      not an invented hole in the completed wall. Lime and crushed pottery are source materials, not a
      modern repair product.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “The work will soon be finished” follows the printed working choice compared with the versions.
      The corresponding Athos word is reported illegible, with a completion suggesting a related finishing
      verb. It is not a fully legible unanimous Greek reading.
  - marker: c
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: “Master” renders the tower owner’s title in this scene. “Sir” elsewhere addresses the shepherd,
      while “the Lord” in the following adjuration remains a divine reference. The explanation later identifies
      the great man as the Son of God.
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The first “everything” translates a bracketed insertion by Harmer compared with the Latin traditions
      and Ethiopic; Athos is reported to omit it. “I must be busy for a little while” translates the supplied
      working Greek, Μικρὸν ἔχω ἀκαιρεθῆναι, which specifies no location. The earlier draft note reported
      a different Athos form for this clause, but the supplied bounded evidence does not identify that
      form or provide the relevant apparatus entry. Its wording and English meaning therefore remain unestablished
      here; the selected working reading is retained pending clarification.
